findings: ctl (S7.15b): ais_3u's rate damping is certified at max |mu| = 1 - 2.5e-13 (the committed result; 1 - 3.0e-13 by the method): a direction the law leaves marginal, judged by the last bits of the arithmetic, inside the tolerance the method is held to. A certificate should not count a multiplier within its numerical tolerance of 1 as inside the unit circle (a stated margin, or such a law judged not certified); ctl's to decide. Transcribed as the tool judged it (strictly below 1).

ctl (S7.15b): the certificate states the flight laws again (fq_torque, as tools/floquet.py did) rather than calling the flight software's own (fsw/pseudocode/05_control.pc), and its own orbit (a circle of 6378137 m plus the altitude, 3.986004418e14) rather than env's; the two copies of each law can drift apart. Calling the flight software's laws and env's constants is ctl's choice.
ctl (S7.15b): the tool refused an LQR or a sliding-mode law (ValueError); the method gives them no torque (fq_torque). The certificate judges only fq_laws' seven, so no answer changed.

translators (S7.15b): a module new to a target rewrites every module of it: each generated module imports every record of the target (`use crate::gen::floquet::{FqGains}` in sizebudget.rs) and the loop counters' names (`__end28`) are numbered across the target, so adding floquet rewrote 11 of adcs-design's modules with no change in what they do. Records imported by the modules that use them, and counters numbered per function, would keep a diff to the module that changed.

translators (S7.15b, fixed): MATLAB's sqrt, asin, acos, log, log10, log2 and pow are complex outside their real domain, where C, Rust and the interpreter give nan, and MATLAB compares a complex number by its real part: the star tracker's st_attitude dropped another star in MATLAB on a vector whose cosine fell below -1 (an acos of a dot product of directions, clamped above only). Fixed in the translator (the runtime's asils.pc.sqrt_ and the rest, nan there; selftest::domain). A design that clamps such a cosine on both sides (sens's st_attitude clamps only above 1) would not lean on it.

tools (S7.15b, fixed): S7.15's evaluate change (no function guessed for a node whose module has several) made the health map refuse 189 method nodes ('its pseudocode defines no function'), which tests/test_design_build.py's health map test caught at 65fcd16; evaluate now says the module names none for the node, which the health map shows open, not refused.

language (S7.15b): a buffer is an inout input only, so `adcs design call floquet::fq_frame` hands back the run's nine columns (17,218 samples each) it only reads; a read-only buffer would save the echo (0.1 s).

act and design: the slew is stated twice: gw_3 and gw_4 (spec/physics/rw.pc: H = 2 I theta/T, tau = 4 I theta/T^2) and the sizing's demand (design/sizedemand.pc, S7.15, as flown: the rate twice the angle over the time, the acceleration 2 pi the angle over the time squared). Engine targets that want a library relation (spec/physics/orbit.pc's circular_period in env_case_orbit) need names scoped to their module in the language (both interpreters, every translator) or the target to call the relations crate.

translator_gaps.G1: Random streams. The models draw from counter-based SplitMix64 streams (Box-Muller, a spare kept). Pseudocode has no 64-bit wrapping integers (band/shl stop at 2^53), so a draw cannot be written. Needs a toolbox stream type and draws (normal, uniform, normal3) in the interpreter and the three translators; MATLAB must do the uint64 arithmetic in two 32-bit halves.
translator_gaps.G2: A proc calling a proc. Device models keep state and call helpers that keep state. Workaround today: state as a record passed in and returned (as the flight software does).
translator_gaps.G3: Arrays of records. Per-rotor state, the star catalogue (direction, magnitude), the pair table, history buffers of (t, q). Workaround: parallel fixed arrays with a count.
translator_gaps.G4: Large arrays by reference. The star-tracker frame (detector_px^2 doubles), its scratch copy, the pair table, the 4000-star catalogue. The translators pass arrays by value (part of the +9 % average, up to +26 %, S6 accepted on small arrays); here it would be prohibitive. Needs inout parameters or a workspace record handed by reference.
translator_gaps.G5: Non-finite values. Models use INFINITY (no spin-down), NEG_INFINITY (never blind) and NaN (not stated). The translators refuse a non-finite literal. Needs inf and nan constants and isfinite / isnan.
translator_gaps.G6: Choices. Kind (rw, fmr, cmg, vscmg), the star-tracker model (noise, quest, image), the Sun-sensor level (model, chain), law names, guidance kinds, initial-attitude kinds, slot names. Needs a choice type declared in the design and written as int constants.
translator_gaps.G7: Sorting and early exit. The centroid median, the brightest-12 selection, the candidate order in select_rotor, the polygon order in section(). No sort, break, continue or return; settle and flags work but are long. A toolbox sort (indices of a fixed array) is the clean way.
translator_gaps.G8: The core and generated code meet. The integrator (core) calls a generated deriv; the step order calls generated device steps. Needs one stable generated signature per model and records the core can use without defining them again.
translator_gaps.G9: Generic units. Helpers such as lag(x, u, tau, dt) serve dipoles, flows and momenta; a function is written for one dimension today.
translator_gaps.G10: Reading files. Product and part descriptors, the catalogue scan in select_rotor. Reading stays toolbox; the relation takes the arrays.
translator_gaps.G11: Speed. The engine runs long scenarios and 4,516-run campaigns; Octave runs the twin. Generated scalar loops in Octave and by-value arrays in Rust and C may cost much. Measure each step; the target is no worse than S6 accepted.
translator_gaps.G12: Named capacities. NR = 8, NG = 4, NC = 6, NH = 2, NS = 8, HIST = 64, GPS_HIST = 256, N_STARS = 4000. An array length is a literal in pseudocode; a named constant length is needed so capacities are stated once.
translator_gaps.G13: Deterministic maths. The engine calls the pure-Rust libm (adcs-sim-core/pm.rs) so a trajectory is the same on every target. The Rust translator already takes a maths module; generated engine code must use it, or trajectories move in the last bits.
translator_gaps.G14: Data tables from the design. Every published model carries data (IGRF 5,070 values, the IAU 2006 series 56,162, the DE440 slice about 9,200 a year). A `const` array works in Rust and C, but MATLAB writes the whole literal at every use (and a MATLAB literal cannot be indexed); nothing says the values are a node's table. Needs a `data` item: a named, typed (real with a unit, or int), 1-D or 2-D array whose values the design writes row by row, emitted once (Rust static, C const, MATLAB a function with a persistent copy) and indexed in place.
translator_gaps.G15: Long series and run-time data. The IAU 2006 series (3,082 terms over 1,309 integer argument rows), Chebyshev (Clenshaw) and Legendre recursions are loops over data (G14 with int data, G12 for their sizes, G4 for scratch by reference). Time series (EOP, space weather, DE440) are embedded as the slice the case's runs span, generated from the design; reading them at run time stays the file readers' work, into the design, never into a model. Speed in Octave (G11) to be measured.
translator_gaps.G16: Run-time sized buffers (found and done at S7.10). The star tracker's frame (detector_px^2 numbers, up to 8,192^2) and pair table (452,404 entries at a 0.17 rad half-angle) are as long as the part makes them. Done: an inout input of a fn may be a buffer of numbers (real[1][*], int[*]), len() its length, read and set by index, handed on, a sized array where one is wanted; Rust a slice, C its address and length, MATLAB the array; vectors at a stated length (## length: N); trinetra-toolbox/5.

options.tndb_binary: Add `tndb read FILE [--engine-inputs|--cases|--node ID]` printing JSON (an array of {path, body}: jsondecode turns keys with / into mangled field names). The binary already carries SQLite (rusqlite bundled) and ships with the application. Works the same in MATLAB and Octave 7+; one process per run, cached in a containers.Map. Measured here: Octave 8.4 decodes all 163 engine inputs (280 kB) in 0.02 s.
options.java_jdbc: Needs a third-party SQLite JDBC driver jar with native libraries on javaclasspath; Octave may run without a JVM. Fragile, not recommended.
options.mex: Needs a C compiler on every user machine and a build per platform and per MATLAB/Octave ABI. Not recommended.
